LIS-A1-06.script: Good morning, everyone. The school music room is open for a short song workshop this Saturday. Please come to Music Room 2 at eleven o'clock. We will practise two easy songs. Bring a pencil. You do not need to bring an instrument because our school has drums and keyboards. The workshop ends at twelve o'clock. To join, write your name on the music list near the office by Friday.

LIS-A2-07.script: Hi! Can you help me choose something to do this weekend? The zip on my school bag is broken, and I'd rather repair the bag than buy a new one. I can only go out on Sunday afternoon, after two. My aunt can come with me. I'd like to be indoors because the weather might be rainy. I don't mind making a small donation, but I don't want to pay a fixed entry fee. Could you tell me which event would be useful? And please let me know if they can definitely fix the bag.

LIS-B1-08.script: I think the Quiet Study Zone is the more practical first pilot. Students have told me that a calm place after class would help them prepare for assessments, and the annex already has desks. Still, we must be careful about the questionnaire. It was sent just before exam week, when students might have been thinking more about silent study than they usually do. I also see the value of a Project Studio for teamwork. Because we can fund only one room, I'd begin with the quiet annex and ask students how often they actually use it. After four weeks, we could collect feedback from students who wanted a project room, too. Then the council would have better evidence before choosing any permanent plan.

reading_asset.body: Riverside Clean-up — Saturday, 9:00–11:00 a.m. Meet at the footbridge. The team provides rubbish bags and gloves. Please wear closed shoes. Seed Swap — Sunday, 10:00–11:00 a.m. Meet at the community garden. Exchange spare seeds or ask for advice about growing plants in small spaces. Entry is free; if you have no seeds, you can still ask questions.

reading_asset.title: School Council: One Room, Eight Weeks
reading_asset.body: The school has enough staff funding to run one eight-week after-school room pilot. The council must select one plan and review its value before asking for a permanent space.   Proposal Q: Quiet Study Zone. The library annex could offer 20 desks on Tuesday and Thursday afternoons. A staff member would supervise independent study. This may help students who cannot work quietly at home. However, group presentations and lively collaboration would not be allowed in this room.   Proposal P: Project Studio. An unused classroom could open on three afternoons each week. Movable tables would support group projects and short presentations. However, supervising equipment and managing noise could cost more staff time.   In a recent questionnaire of 100 students, 62 selected an interest in quiet study and 51 selected an interest in group projects. Students could select both interests, so the figures must not be added together as if the two groups were separate. The questionnaire gives useful feedback but does not prove how many students would attend either room regularly.
